dataset.name: pm-checkpoint2-example-records
dataset.description: Two complete teaching-example records (one per textbook track) delivered for PM checkpoint 2, including the CORRECTED bilingual bridge example (शाळा is Marathi; Hindi for school is विद्यालय). These records conform to curriculum.schema.json v1.1.0 and are appended to the main example bank only after PM review.

missJulieTurns.text: Very good! You said शाळा — that is Marathi, and it is a beautiful word for it.
missJulieTurns.ttsNote: Warm acceptance; do not flag as an error.

missJulieTurns.text: Marathi madhye mhaṇatat शाळा; Hindi mein vidyalay kehte hain. Aur English mein — school. Can you say school?
missJulieTurns.ttsNote: The PM bridge pattern (accept → attribute each home language CORRECTLY → request). The turn names both home languages; शाळा is explicitly attributed to Marathi per the checkpoint-2 correction.

missJulieTurns.text: School! Shabash. Tomorrow when you come in, tell me one thing you see at school.

examples.intent: Accept the home-language answer, attribute it to the CORRECT home language, then request the English word. Corrects the checkpoint-1 draft where शाळा was mislabelled as Hindi.
examples.masteryCheck: INDEPENDENT_ANSWERING: later in the same session Miss Julie points at the school picture and asks 'What is this?' with no model — 'school' must come without the bridge. DELAYED_RECALL: the tomorrow line above checks it survives overnight.

review.note: Syllabus alignment verified against the official PDF word bank (printed p.1). This is NOT teacher approval; pedagogyStatus remains DRAFT_PENDING_TEACHER_REVIEW.

missJulieTurns.text: छान, Salman-कडून सुरुवात! माझं नाव — in English: My name is…
missJulieTurns.ttsNote: Marathi-first acceptance, then the English frame. Non-English-medium track: Marathi is the bridge, never a failure.

missJulieTurns.text: My name is Salma. Your turn — say the whole line!
Wonderful! Now YOU ask me — What is your name?
(after the child asks) My name is Miss Julie. Glad to meet you, Salma!
missJulieTurns.ttsNote: Teacher deliberately becomes the answerer so the child practises the QUESTION too.

examples.intent: On the non-English-medium track, accept the Marathi answer, hand over the English frame, and reverse roles so the child produces the question — the book's own chain-drill pattern (For the Teacher note, printed p.2).
examples.masteryCheck: INDEPENDENT_ANSWERING: a peer-pair exchange with no teacher model in which the child both asks 'What is your name?' and answers it. DELAYED_RECALL: next session's attendance game — child answers the roll with 'My name is ___' unprompted.

review.note: Frame and activity verified against My English Book printed p.2 (I am Jaya. / My name is Kiran.; chain drill). NOT teacher approval; pedagogyStatus remains DRAFT_PENDING_TEACHER_REVIEW.
